summary: Laryngeal obstruction: Obstruction of the larynx by a foreign body. The mucosa of the superior larynx is very sensitive, so a foreign body normally causes immediate explosive coughing; if that reflex is slowed or absent, choking follows.

evidence.quote: The mucosa of the superior larynx is very sensitive, so a foreign body causes immediate explosive coughing. If that reflex is slowed or absent, choking follows.

summary: Laryngeal cancer: A tumour of the larynx whose spread follows the lymphatics: one confined to the vocal cord spreads late and has a good outlook, while a supraglottic tumour reaches the internal jugular nodes early. The three compartments of the larynx are therefore staged separately.

evidence.quote: No lymphatics at the cords → glottic cancer spreads late (good prognosis); supraglottic cancer spreads early.

summary: Respiratory and cardiovascular centres: The centres for breathing and cardiovascular control, located in the medulla oblongata, which is why compression or a lesion of the medulla is life-threatening.

summary: Paramedian position of the vocal cord: A position of the vocal cord between abduction and adduction, in which the cord of the affected side lies and does not vibrate after damage to the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

summary: Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury: Damage to the recurrent laryngeal nerve, often accidental during partial thyroidectomy. summary: Posterior cricoarytenoid muscle: The intrinsic muscle that is the only dilator of the glottis and the only abductor of the vocal cords, inserting on the muscular process of the arytenoid. It is called the safety muscle of the larynx: if it is paralysed the adductors take the upper hand and the person might die from lack of air.

evidence.quote: Posterior cricoarytenoids are the only abductors: the safety muscles of the larynx.

summary: Thyroidectomy: An operation, named in the lecture as partial thyroidectomy, during which the recurrent laryngeal nerve is often damaged accidentally.

summary: Vocal nodule: An inflammatory nodule that develops in people who overuse the voice at the junction of the anterior one third and posterior two thirds of the vocal cords, the area of maximum contact during vibration.
